body:
Full-codebase review, Android finding. Verified: `grep -rn "withTransaction|@Transaction|runInTransaction"` over the whole module returns nothing.

Every read-modify-write runs unguarded: the sync merge (`upsert(mergeItem(getById(id), dto))`) and every user edit in ItemsRepo/ListsRepo (`getById` -> `upsert`). They run concurrently, because the list screen syncs every 5 s while it is open. A tap that lands between the merge's read and its write is overwritten by the merge writing back the pre-tap row — whole-row, so the field clocks never see the edit and nothing is queued.

Scenario: a shopper checks an item off exactly while a background sync applies that row; the row flips back to todo and the edit is gone.

Fix direction: wrap each row's merge and each repo `updateField` in `appDb.withTransaction { }`.
title: Android: no database transactions, so a sync merge can silently overwrite a concurrent edit
